title: Balance at the Equinox

before.title: Balance at the Equinox
before.text: The word equinox suggests equal night, but daylight and darkness are not exactly twelve hours everywhere on that date. The Sun is a disk rather than a point, and Earth's atmosphere bends its light. Sunrise is defined by the first visible edge of the Sun, while sunset uses the last edge. Together, these effects make daylight slightly longer.

after.text: The word equinox suggests equal night, but daylight and darkness are not exactly twelve hours everywhere on that date. Together, these effects make daylight slightly longer.

reason: The equinox claim is supported by the US Naval Observatory: solar disk size and atmospheric refraction make sunrise-to-sunset time slightly more than twelve hours in ordinary circumstances. Upper-edge sunrise and sunset definitions are correctly described.
